items.title: Honkai: Star Rail – Log In After Version 4.8 To Claim Astra Yao For Free
items.summary: Following the Zenless Zone Zero special program that revealed HSR's Robin being free as a part of the collab, developer HoYoverse followed up with announcing that ZZZ's Astra Yao being free in Honkai: Star Rail.
items.content:
Following the Zenless Zone Zero special program that revealed HSR’s Robin being free as a part of the collab, developer HoYoverse followed up with announcing that ZZZ’s Astra Yao being free in Honkai: Star Rail. All players have to do is log in after the Version 4.8 update launches and until Version 5.0 is over to claim a free copy!

In ZZZ, Robin is the newest S-rank Ether Defense unit. While in HSR, Astra Yao is the latest 5-star Quantum Harmony addition to the game. We don’t yet know much about her kit and who she will support outside of Ellen (which is a given, considering the Fate collab trend), so stay tuned!

HoYoverse’s Honkai: Star Rail and Zenless Zone Zero are having collabs in which the games are exchanging some heroes. In the upcoming Version 3.4 ZZZ gets Robin (S-rank Ether Defense) and Kafka (S-rank Electric Anomaly) , while HSR will be receiving Astra Yao (5-star Quantum Harmony) and Ellen Joe (5-star Ice Destruction) in the future update 4.8.

In an amusing move, both songstresses will be joining the roster for free – at least in the M0W0/E0S0 version. How useful will they prove to be is for the future Versions to nail.

items.title: What’s Next After Five Years of HoYoverse
items.summary: After five years of existence, HoYoverse is aiming to support as many as nine live service games at the same time.
items.content:
Somewhere in Seoul, South Korea, to celebrate five years of HoYoverse, the international division operating under Chinese developer miHoYo, I’m being briefed on the overwhelming success of its robust games portfolio, which includes hits like Genshin Impact and Honkai: Star Rail . What’s more, I’m also shown some upcoming titles, such as Petit Planet , through which the studio is seeking to capture players across new gaming verticals.

The beginning of HoYoverse is strongly linked to the worldwide attention that the aforementioned Genshin Impact , a free-to-play Breath of the Wild -like, has been receiving since it was first announced back in 2019. Seven years on, Genshin is arguably still HoYoverse’s flagship, and there are no signs of stopping soon, even though Snezhnaya, the supposed final nation, was added to the game this past summer. In fact, in the words of Sam Lai, lead of Global Public Relations Communication at HoYoverse, there are “more adventures ahead” for the more than 300 million reported global users .

Not to be outdone by Genshin , Honkai: Star Rail , a turn-based RPG and spiritual successor to Honkai Impact 3rd (which is still live), has recently, in Version 4.7, wrapped up a major story arc and introduced Aha, a higher-dimensional god known as an Aeon, as a playable character. When asked about why now is the right time to give players the keys to such a powerful figure in the game’s lore, Lead Game Designer Chegnan An told me that “she’s the first one due to her being the most human-like.”

As for whether or not more Aeons would be entering the fray in the near future, An made sure to not divulge too much, but he did confess that worlds usually take more than 15 months to be added to the game and that, in the next year or so, players will be able to see some of the figures they’ve been wanting for a long time.

“When it comes to the theme of each world”, An continues, “it’s not just about the concept of a certain culture but more about how to introduce our stories and characters.” To illustrate this point, he gives The Xianzhou Luofu as an example, which is “not just about a Chinese-style planet” but is also“a way to introduce the Paths of Hunt and Abundance,” which can shape characters’ combat roles and factions.

Furthermore, An emphasizes that he, as a developer, also wants to explore some modern-day issues together with players through the stories Star Rail tells and the worlds within which they unfold. Lastly, on the topic of the worldwide appeal of the game, which has upwards of 5M players logging in daily , An is keen to highlight the “exclusiveness” and “uniqueness” of the worldbuilding and the characters’ personalities which, when put together, make for an “immersive experience.”

HoYoverse would follow up the launch of Honkai: Star Rail in 2023 with Zenless Zone Zero — an action title in the vein of something like Bayonetta — which was released in the summer of 2024 to largely positive reviews. Although admittedly not as much of a home run as either of the two previous titles, ZZZ proved successful in its own right, surpassing $600 USD in revenue as of July of this year (despite a %51 decline in second-year spending) and being nominated for Best Mobile Game at both gamescom and The Game Awards .

Nevertheless, ZZZ has been receiving a plethora of updates, with the most recent one being Version 3.3 “Journey To The Sky”, the twenty-first major release since 2024. Today also brought an announcement that ZZZ’s 3.4 release is set for December 2nd. Beyond the two brand-new S-Rank characters, Phoenix and Severian, players can also look forward to the continuation of the events in the district of Booastrum as well as a handful of limited-time events such as “Spooky Funhouse Tales” and a “Bang Boo” rescue mission.

Now, whereas ZZZ is HoYoverse’s most recent title to date, there are already plans for games releasing in the near future. First up is Petit Planet , a life simulator with a striking similarity to Nintendo’s Animal Crossing: New Horizons . My colleague, Jordan, was glowing in his preview published this summer and, after spending around two hours with the upcoming title myself, I, too, think it will make for a delightful, if familiar, experience. So far, my biggest reservation has to do with the game’s monetization.

Indeed, the gacha/capsule-toy monetization practices that are so prevalent across all of HoYoverse’s products will be present in the otherwise cozy world of Petit Planet , with the important distinction that, according to the developers, it will be limited exclusively to cosmetics instead of character unlocks. We’ll be able to assess to what extent this inclusion will harm this title, especially considering the relaxing atmosphere it seeks to conjure, with release on mobile and PC on December 4 and on Nintendo Switch 2 sometime in 2027.

Until then, Petit Planet Lead Game Designer “Murphy” and Lead Artist Yinli Huang were happy to share some insights into their process and answer some pressing questions. From the get-go, Murphy explains, the game seeks to give every player “a home that is unmistakably yours” and connect them together “without a single word exchanged.” In fact, it was early in development that she and her team came to the realization that players “want quality without grind, competition or performance”. As such, Murphy elaborates, Petit Planet is “not a game about escaping life”. Rather, the point is to shape a “gentle world waiting for you after you’ve taken care of real life.”

As opposed to the other HoYoverse entries, Petit Planet is also aimed at families and younger audiences, which, for one, very much comes across through the art design and philosophy. “We made the deliberate choice to keep the visuals slightly imperfect”, Huang admits. This is because, in his view, “imperfection is what makes players slow down and notice the moment.” With regard to the obvious visual comparisons to Animal Crossing and the planet design reminiscent of Super Mario Galaxy , both Murphy and Huang refrain from addressing these two Nintendo games entirely.

Instead, Murphy mentions that she was inspired by both The Little Prince , the celebrated children’s short story which follows the titular prince as he travels from planet to planet in search of meaning and a deeper understanding of love, and… Clarkson’s Farm . Yes, you read that right. As it seems, Petit Planet draws inspiration from the British documentary series about ongoing events at the farm of former Top Gear host Jeremy Clarkson, situated in a beautiful English region called The Cotswolds. Stranger things have happened.

In any case, HoYoverse’s ambition does not stop with Petit Planet for Honkai: Nexus Anima , the company’s own take on creature catching and yet another entry in the Honkai franchise, is set for a worldwide final beta release on mobile and PC on November 25. Unfortunately, I did not get hands-on time with the game myself, but my colleague, Matt, played it over the summer and was really impressed, if overwhelmed, by the opening hours.

items.title: Zenless Zone Zero Honkai: Star Rail Crossover Starts With 3.4 in December
items.summary: December kicks off with the 3.4 Zenless Zone Zero update with 2 Honkai: Star Rail characters and the Sunbringer launch.
items.content:
HoYoVerse confirmed the 3.4 release date for the patch and version update that adds the Zenless Zone Zero Honkai: Star Rail crossover event and new three-in-one Agent character Sunbringer . It appears on December 2, 2026.

The first half of the update will include the S-Rank Agents Sunbringer and Robin banners until January 12, 2027. The second half’s banners run January 1-21, 2027 and include Kafka and an Alice rerun. (They’re both S-Rank units too.) During the patch, people can get Robin for free by logging in during the update and claiming her. She’ll come with custom Drive Discs. (An end-date wasn’t mentioned for that promotion.) The in-game store will also sell the Moonlit Promenade outfit for Sunbringer and Cosmic Beat one for Robin.

Here’s the 3.4 “The Finality of the Day” trailer for Zenless Zone Zero that goes over the update. It begins with an extended teaser for the story for this chapter and the Sunbringer gameplay teaser. After that, it shows the Honkai: Star Rail Zenless Zone Zero crossover by suggesting somehow Sparkle maybe was involved in Kafka and Robin being “isekai-ed” into this game. The new engines and events are also teased, including ones to give people more Polychromes. It also confirmed that the S-Rank Agents Ju Fufu and Vivian both get Agent enhancements in this update.

And the full HoYoVerse Special Program discussing all the details about the update and crossover can be watched below.

HoYoVerse also announced a new official Zenless Zone Zero tool. People can log in to see their Signal Search records and check the Signal Search Statistical Tool for data on their past gacha pulls.

Zenless Zone Zero is available for the PS5, Xbox Series X, PC, and mobile devices and gets Sunbringer and the Honkai: Star Rail crossover in 3.4 starting on December 2, 2026.

items.title: "Zenless Zone Zero Version 3.4 "The Finality of the Day" Launches December 2, Alongside the Honkai: Star Rail Crossover"
items.summary: 'The Finality of the Day' version 3.4 update out next month to coincide with 'Honkai: Star Rail' collaboration.
items.content:
SINGAPORE, November 20, 2026 — HoYoverse, a global interactive entertainment brand, announced today that Version 3.4 "The Finality of the Day" of its urban fantasy ARPG Zenless Zone Zero will launch on December 2. The story of the Sky Island of Roscaelifer reaches its final climax, as Sunbringer, a new Void Hunter and the first Enchainer Agent, joins the fight. The new version also kicks off the Zenless Zone Zero × Honkai: Star Rail collaboration, introducing two crossover Agents, Robin and Kafka, along with themed events. It also brings new combat gameplay, updates to permanent game modes, and a variety of version rewards. Click to view Zenless Zone Zero's latest trailer for Version 3.4: https://youtu.be/oSNwzOoxpM4 In Version 3.4, Roscaelifer's main story is about to reach its climax. From the Bangboo corruption incident to High Ambitions Corp.'s invasion, the Proxies and their allies have weathered crisis after crisis together. Now, the enemy has stepped out of the shadows, and Roscaelifer faces a decisive battle for its very survival. For the first time, the three Sunbringers — Dracaene, Lindverne, and Eldreda—will fight side-by-side, joining the Proxies to take on a formidable foe and defend Roscaelifer. New characters and menacing enemies are taking the stage, while the arrival of an unexpected character leaves even more mysteries hanging over this new chapter. How will this storm change the fate of the Celestial Nexus? What trials await the Proxies and their allies? All will be revealed in "The Finality of the Day." Once this version update goes live, Sunbringer, leader of Roscaelifer, joins the fray as an S-Rank Genesis Flare Armorer Agent, bringing a unique offensive and defensive rhythm through a three-member synergistic combat style: Eldreda, Lindverne, and Dracaene take turns stepping in with a lance, greatsword, and shield, seamlessly balancing offense and defense. Their Armorer attacks can stack Gash on enemies, and consuming Gash triggers Maim while building up Wishfire. Once Wishfire is sufficient, Eldreda can hold Basic Attack to hurl her lance and make her entrance, following up with a synergy Chain Attack. When Decibels are sufficient, they can unleash a two-stage Ultimate that detonates all Embermark stacks on the enemy at once, triggering Emberburst for massive damage. When the new version launches, Proxies can obtain Sunbringer and the S-Rank Armorer W-Engine Dragonfire Mirage via Signal Search. On top of that, the new Bangboo Sleepwalkerboo will also arrive in the Bangboo Channel, summoning Bangboo soldiers to back you up in combat and boosting Sunbringer's damage when Sunbringer is on the squad. The two crossover Agents also bring their own distinct combat styles. Robin can keep up her Concerto performance off-field, granting teammates shields while boosting their DEF and DMG, and can extend her support effects by re-entering the field. Her Ultimate can also restore Sharpness for Armorer Agents. Meanwhile, Kafka, an S-Rank Electric Agent, builds her offense around Attribute Anomalies and Disorder DMG. While in the Hunter's Overture state, she can choose between slashing or shooting attacks, enhancing direct DMG or speeding up Attribute Anomaly buildup, respectively. When her slashes hit an enemy afflicted with an Attribute Anomaly, she can also trigger a Lightning Surge to deal additional DMG. Robin's brand-new outfit, Cosmic Beat, will also be made available. Sunbringer's and Robin's Signal Search channels will open on the first day of the update and run throughout Version 3.4, while Kafka will arrive in the second half of the version. As for reruns, the S-Rank Physical Anomaly Agent Alice and the S-Rank Anomaly W-Engine Practiced Perfection will return in the second half of the version. Beyond combat, Dracaene, Lindverne, and Eldreda will each have their own Trust Events, showcasing the distinct daily lives of the three Sunbringers. Once all three reach max trust level, Proxies will also unlock a special side quest to help secretly plan their birthday party. Their new daily wear outfit, Moonlit Promenade, reveals a side of the three Sunbringers as they step into city life, letting Proxies experience up close Dracaene's gentle sweetness, Lindverne's playful personality, and Eldreda's bold, free-spirited charm. The Moonlit Promenade outfit set and its matching Starlit Stroll Limited Gift will also be available. The latter includes a three-person Accompany Experience and an exclusive Idle Action, so Proxies can enjoy their everyday company on the streets of New Eridu. A dynamic wallpaper and three matching Inter-Knot avatars will also arrive with this version. As for events, the collab event "Lost in a Theatrical Dream" between Zenless Zone Zero and Honkai: Star Rail kicks off in Version 3.4. Proxies will team up with Robin, Kafka, and their New Eridu companions to film a series, featuring stealth raids and Agent interactions. Complete the event to score rewards like the collab Bangboo Pom-Pom and Polychromes. On top of that, the new version also brings the "Opening Act: Enter the Knight" combat mode and a new "Dark Dungeon Survival" season for Enigma of the Labyrinth. Proxies can join in to earn Polychromes, a profile icon, new accessories, and more. As for rewards, after the Version 3.4 update, log in to claim the limited collab S-Rank Agent Robin for free, along with the upgrade materials needed to raise her to Lv. 40 and a full set of Drive Discs with matching Main Stats. During the version, Proxies will also receive overclock materials for the W-Engine Twilight Afterimage and all remaining Agent Focus: Pyrois for free, and check-in and web events will be available. To thank Proxies around the world for sticking with us, starting January 1, Proxies can claim up to 1,600 Polychromes in total through daily login check-ins. During the version, Zenless Zone Zero will also partner with Make-A-Wish on a charitable initiative, inviting the community to join Sunbringer in helping support wishes for children with critical illnesses. The "Filmgoer Thank-You Gift" cumulative top-up event will also run during the version. Proxies can earn commemorative ticket stubs by purchasing Monochromes or the New Eridu City Fund, Inter-Knot Membership, or cash bundles. Collect enough ticket stubs to unlock rewards such as an S-Rank Agent and W-Engine of your choice. Kafka's signature W-Engine Requiem Araneae will also be available in the W-Engine selection pool. The event also offers personalized rewards, including a Sunbringer-themed animated namecard, a sidebar theme and pendant, and collab-themed accessories. Zenless Zone Zero Version 3.4 "The Finality of the Day" will launch on December 2, 2026, on PlayStation®5, PlayStation®5 Pro, Xbox Series X|S, Xbox Cloud Gaming, PC, iOS, and Android, and Steam on PC. The game is rated Teen by the ESRB and is also classified as PEGI 16. For more information, please visit the official website at https://zenless.hoyoverse.com/ or follow @ZZZ_EN on X (Twitter). About Zenless Zone Zero Zenless Zone Zero is HoYoverse's urban fantasy ARPG, in which a calamity called the "Hollows" has destroyed modern society. New Eridu, the last remaining metropolis, has risen against the odds amidst this destructive catastrophe to become the last bastion of modern civilization. In the game, players assume the role of a "Proxy" accompanied by unique characters as they explore Hollows, battle enemies, complete commissions, and reveal the mysteries behind New Eridu. About HoYoverse HoYoverse is committed to providing immersive virtual world experiences to players around the world. We have brought fans popular games including Genshin Impact, Honkai: Star Rail, Honkai Impact 3rd, Tears of Themis, and Zenless Zone Zero, as well as a wide range of entertainment content. Our community is at the heart of everything we do. We are devoted to engaging fans and fostering an enthusiastic and inclusive global community that provides access and encouragement for people to share their passion for ACG (Animation, Comics, and Games) through their own creativity and skills. Pushing the boundaries of imagination, we consistently explore cutting-edge game development technologies and have accumulated leading technical capabilities in cel shading, cloud gaming, and other fields. In the future, we will continue to expand our content production, technology research, and publishing duties through operations in offices in Singapore, Montreal, Los Angeles, Tokyo, Seoul, and other regions.

items.title: Silver Wolf, Acheron and Jing Yuan Among Six Characters Returning in Honkai: Star Rail 4.7
items.summary: Honkai: Star Rail 4.7 brings back six limited five-stars, three in each half of the version. The update, “Now, Lay Laughter to All Stars,” went live on November 11, 2026. Its reruns are an odd but useful mix: three fairly new Elation characters first, then three damage dealers who’ve been around for years. Phase 1 […]
items.content:
Honkai: Star Rail 4.7 brings back six limited five-stars, three in each half of the version. The update, “Now, Lay Laughter to All Stars,” went live on November 11, 2026. Its reruns are an odd but useful mix: three fairly new Elation characters first, then three damage dealers who’ve been around for years.

Phase 1 has Silver Wolf LV.999, Sparxie and Yao Guang. Phase 2 has Acheron, Jing Yuan and Dan Heng • Imbibitor Lunae. All six share the spotlight with Aha, the Aeon of Elation, who’s the version’s new limited five-star.

The first half started on launch day and ends on December 2. Until then, you can pull for Silver Wolf LV.999, Sparxie or Yao Guang.

All three are on the Path of Elation, the same Path as Aha. That matters, because HoYoverse describes Aha’s kit as one that strengthens Elation and unlocks unique abilities for other Elation characters on the team. So if you want a full Elation team built around the new Aeon, all three possible partners are on banners at the same time. Silver Wolf LV.999 is an Imaginary damage dealer, Sparxie is Fire, and Yao Guang was set up as the main support for Elation teams.

Aha’s own banner, “A Comedy of Stars,” has Asta, Lynx and Yukong as its boosted four-stars, and it stays up for the whole version. Each phase also gets its own five-star Light Cone banners, and the boosted four-star Light Cones don’t change between the two phases.

The second half swaps the Elation trio for three of the game’s best-known attackers. Jing Yuan and Dan Heng • Imbibitor Lunae have both been around since the game’s first year, and Acheron, a Nihility character, arrived later.

This time there’s something new attached. Version 4.7 adds Affinitive Eidolons, which give extra combat abilities to certain characters once you unlock them. HoYoverse picked these same three as the first to get them. So for a lot of players, Phase 2 is the first real look at how the new system changes characters they may have been using for years.

There’s a free option too. Anyone at Trailblaze Level 4 or higher can claim Acheron, Dan Heng • Imbibitor Lunae or Jing Yuan for free during 4.7. If you already own all three, the bigger decision is probably whether to pull for extra Eidolons. If you’re newer, the free pick is an easy way to get one of the game’s older stars.

The banners stretch across roughly six weeks, so it’s worth planning your pulls. Stellar Jade is the main currency for Warps, and you get it from story content, events and daily play. Oneiric Shards, which you buy in the in-game shop, can be exchanged for it.

The 4.7 events help a bit. In The Fluffy Movie: Overheated, you work in Aha’s dessert shop to collect Gold Coins. Phantasia Showstage gives out Aha’s limited Star Lotto outfit, and Interastral Peace Gala: Road to Fame is a new combat challenge. Currency Wars, the permanent mode, also starts its second season, “Voyage Into the Canvas.”

If you’re buying Oneiric Shards, the in-game store and the platform stores are the official routes. Some players also use honkai star rail top up listings from third-party marketplaces. Either way, the in-game store’s prices are the ones to compare against.

All of this happens during the last chapter of Planarcadia. An ancient leviathan called the Voracity wakes up after being sealed for over a thousand Amber Eras, and Aha stages the Final Phantasmoon Games aboard the Starfroster, a ship shaped like a cake, to use as bait. The arc ends with a new song, “Ex Nihilo,” and HoYoverse put out a new animated short on launch day.

There’s also a crossover coming. HoYoverse says Ellen and Astra Yao from Zenless Zone Zero arrive in Version 4.8. General marketplaces such as LootBar list Honkai: Star Rail alongside other HoYoverse games like Genshin Impact.

Before any of that, December 2 is the date to watch. That’s when the Phase 1 banners close and Acheron, Jing Yuan and Dan Heng • Imbibitor Lunae come back, with their Affinitive Eidolons ready to unlock.

items.title: 13 tips you need to know before starting Honkai: Star Rail
Hands on with the Honkai: Star Rail v4.0 experience
Honkai: Star Rail 4.0 impressions
items.content:
I'll admit, I recently burned out on Honkai: Star Rail. Upon hearing the news that 3.8 would be the lengthiest patch yet and with content more sparse than ever before, I decided to take a break for the first time since I started playing all the way back in 1.0. The entire Amphoreus saga left me feeling drained; I thoroughly enjoyed 3.0-3.4 as excellent set-up chapters, but felt lost as the plot became a labyrinth of hidden motivations, layered twists, hours of exposition, and endless proper nouns. When looking at the story as a whole, I love the characters (Aglaea and Anaxa in particular) and the rich history of the world within the Scepter, but the later patches often felt like studying for a needlessly convoluted test. I understood the gist of what was happening, but I won't lie to you and say I could describe to you in detail what Cyrene's deal is or how Evernight fits into everything.

All that's to say: I was looking forward to the Astral Express crew taking a well-earned vacation to Planarcadia, the planet of Elation. Despite two of the game's four current versions ostensibly beginning with Akivili's disciples deciding that they need a break from the backbreaking work of saving the universe, neither has resulted in our trailblazers seeing much downtime. Unlike previous excursions, it's all hands on deck: everyone gets off at this stop (save for Black Swan's incredibly hasty and unfortunate exit prior to departure). It's fun to see the entire main cast get involved, none more welcome than Himeko — up until now, the only character trait I could've told you about her was that she's terrible at making coffee. Getting some elaboration on her backstory and giving her a personality outside of "Express mom" is long overdue.

The Trailblazer and March 7th begin their Planarcadian getaway with a suitably devious greeting by none other than our old pal Sparkle. We're given a tour of the vibrant, totally-not-Japanese-inspired streets, crawling with humans living in tentative harmony with totally-not-Penaconian-memetic-entities known as imagenae. Here, we catch a glimpse of what I hope will become one of Planarcadia's core themes: gentrification and the plight of capitalism, with a side of anti-imperialism (all perpetrated by the IPC, of course). It's bold, though, and I worry that future patches will keep these criticisms in the background rather than highlight them as Planarcadia's core issues. I would love so much for little nuggets of lore to be elaborated upon, ones that suggest a more serious political history than Aha would have you believe: what did the imagenae do before the IPC forced them to integrate into society? Were they not allowed to work at all? Were they marginalized and seen as second-class citizens? Is the Department of Aberration Defense an inherently evil organization left to determine on their own which imagenae deserve their continued existence and which do not? Is Kuchiba so hot that it doesn't even matter?

This brings us to the Synwish Syndicate, a gang formerly designed to be a respite for imagenae that feel rejected elsewhere, now, due to IPC intervention, a gang that largely exists to enable monetary gain by questionable means. Here at the syndicate's headquarters, the plot quickly begins to balloon into what feels like a collection of introductions for what's to come. We have Pearl's cold and calculating grip on the planet, Himeko and her confounding family history, the potential return of the Herald of Death, the Stellaron Hunters' unknown involvement in the Phantasmoon Games, Sunday's inadvertent entry into the Games, Evanescia's whole...thing, and Yao Guang's bottomless supply of divinations. What's most shocking is that the patch still manages to pull off a fun (if bloated) self-contained story, adding layers to one of HSR's most inscrutable characters and ending things with one of the game's best low-stakes twists.

I'm no Xianzhou Arbiter-General, but I can pretty easily peer into the future and divine a prophecy for Honkai: Star Rail: each new patch will introduce and/or discuss at length a new prophecy that cryptically divulges the fate of a character and/or planet and/or simulation masquerading as a planet. It's hard to pinpoint the moment a theme becomes a crutch, but I think HSR passed that moment long ago. In this patch, we have not one, not two, but three central characters that are defined by their relationship with prophecy and prediction — Yao Guang, Pearl, and the perennial mystery that is Elio and his script. So many in-game conversations devolve into the interpretation of prophecy, and frankly, it's becoming exhausting. We went through an entire version in which each Chrysos Heir had a poetically vague predetermined fate, and before that (and in 3.8's ret-con-y confusion) we had Sparkle's ambiguous "three deaths" for Firefly.

If this were a wholesale replacement for well-executed foreshadowing, we would have a far bigger issue. It's obvious, though, that the writing team knows how to tell a story sans-prophecy, evident in Sparkle's character-driven narrative in this very patch. Sparxie being the "true" Sparkle (as much as old Sparkle is also the "true" Sparkle) is teased so perfectly; the reveal is obvious in retrospect while being difficult to predict with the given information. It's consistently groan-inducing to see this writing cheat code being used ad nauseam within a story that could function better without it. I hope I'll be proven wrong and the game will subvert the words of its murky prophets, leaving me with egg on my face come the conclusion of this leg of the Express' journey.

4.0 is a promising new beginning, and has at the very least brought me back in terms of its story. Though there is an abundance of new proper nouns to memorize and a bevy of new and returning cast members to keep track of, the patch still takes on a welcome return to simplicity and levity (save for the shocking tonal shift right at the end, RIP the Synwish Syndicate Feb. 2026 - Feb. 2026). As long as things don't get too bogged down in extensive metaphors and tiresome exposition, I'm hopeful that Planarcadia can become the most focused version of HSR we've seen so far.
